title: Unsynchronized Access to Correlated Fields
pattern: Multiple struct fields that are tightly correlated (represent a single atomic update) are written to and read from as separate, independent primitive fields without a synchronization lock or transactional barrier.
why_bad: Concurrency hazard. A reader thread can read the fields while an update is in progress, observing an inconsistent partial snapshot (e.g. a new `meas_1` but old `meas_2` and `meas_3`). This leads to "fatally confused" threads and invariant violations.
detection: A set of fields in a struct are modified together in a write routine but are accessed individually by other threads without a lock, atomic snapshot, or RCU boundary.
